title: Maintainability Hygiene
current_summary: Maintainability and local readability are judged through bounded reconstruction inside sound architecture, not mechanical cleanup. Module size, package surfaces, and module headers are inspection signals, not findings by themselves: split or add structure only on concrete responsibility, ownership, unstable-package-surface, reconstruction, or validation-locality evidence, and preserve cohesive long operations where extraction would increase non-local reasoning. The three-family Human Readability investigation validated this (XRef operation.py ~516 LOC and dense_axes.py ~411 LOC are cohesive and locally reconstructable).
next_action: Apply the bounded-reconstruction questions in ordinary reviews; open implementation only on concrete reader/ownership cost plus explicit authority. Add module headers where they give real orientation, not as a uniform mandate; do not run a mechanical cleanup wave. A Human Readability Guide or Sentinel experiment requires separate authorization.
notes: Many low/medium findings are heatmap signals for this concern rather than individual tasks. Reconciled 2026-08-04 with the three-family Human Readability evidence (REVSET-TOPIC-HUMAN-READABILITY, DEC-HUMAN-READABILITY-BOUNDED-RECONSTRUCTION): LOC alone is not a finding, and the module-size/modularization/header FTR records (FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULARIZATION-P4A, FTR-REVIEW-001-MODULE-HEADERS-P5, FTR-MAINTAINER-ENTRYPOINTS-AND-MODULE-BUDGETS-P5) were narrowed accordingly. Real package-surface, ownership, unrelated-responsibility, and agent read-window concerns remain valid.

title: Domain Boundary Robustness
current_summary: An accepted repository-wide policy fixes how far a domain boundary must defend against malformed or unusual input: robust handling of values reasonably implied by the pandas/NumPy/configuration/metadata/artifact contract, but no promise to contain arbitrary hostile executable Python already in-process; a load-bearing framework-vs-workflow-builder responsibility split; and an enforceable review policy that blocks silent threat-model expansion. ADR-TRUSTED-RUNTIME-AND-POLICY-AUTHORITY (Independent Architecture Review 002, accepted 0 Blocking/0 Important/0 Minor) now extends this into runtime/operator trust: a fixed trusted-runtime/operator precondition; independent payload-trust and pipeline-description-trust dimensions with all four combinations representable; operator-owned security policy supplied outside untrusted pipeline input, narrowing-only; per-policy-kind combination/rejection semantics with a capability-activation timing invariant (safe authorization-preparation normalization is permitted before the decision, activation must wait for it); and sink-capability ownership kept separate from payload normalization. No public profile names, policy API, parser/resource limits, or ingress mechanism are adopted; the accepted Trusted Ingress concept remains explanatory only for those. BUG-UNRESOLVED-HELPER-VALUE-NAN-SEMANTICS-P4A is now Done: the carrier defect is fixed, and the semantic contract is accepted and adopted (Semantic Contract Review 001) -- the derived FK-helper cell is presentation only, never resolution authority; an unresolved lookup and a legitimately resolved empty target value may both display "" while remaining fully distinguishable through the authoritative source FK plus `validate_fk_helpers`; no distinct unresolved-value representation, sentinel, or new type was needed. A separate, narrower residual discovered while resolving that BUG -- a resolved FK whose target payload is itself a missing carrier can still reach the ODS renderer's NaN-blind emptiness check and be serialized as literal "nan" -- was transferred, not left implicit, to BUG-ODS-MISSING-CARRIER-LITERAL-NAN-RENDERING-P4A, which is now also Done: a local, `pd.isna`-aware carrier predicate at the ODS renderer boundary closes both independently reproduced trigger shapes (a resolved FK-helper lookup whose target payload is missing, and an ordinary non-FK csv_dir column), with literal domain `"nan"`, legitimate `""`, and XLSX all confirmed unaffected. No known carrier leak remains open at this boundary. `FTR-MINIMAL-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A` (New, decision-ready; a431182) recorded the Phase-D current-state inventory and recommended MVP category set (String/Boolean/Number/Missing, Error deferred; Integer-vs-Float bounded-deferred) with no runtime, ADR, or Project Memory change of its own. A follow-up scope-hygiene pass (0f07368) then tightened that FTR's formula and Date/Time wording and split a dedicated deferred anchor, `FTR-FORMULA-INGRESS-ROUNDTRIP-WHITELIST-P5`, for durable formula-preservation/roundtrip constraints (strict allowlist, feature-owned contracts, no general Excel/OpenFormula compatibility promise, the FK-helper emit-does-not-imply-preserve precedent) so a future implementation agent cannot accidentally widen Slice 1 into formula support. Phase D's Minimal Internal Value Model Slice 1 (D1-D3 in `FTR-MINIMAL-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A`) is now independently accepted: Independent Review 001 accepted it with three Important follow-up findings (IVM-REVIEW-F1/F2/F3), the implementer resolved all three in two follow-up commits, and a fresh, independent follow-up review (Review Pass 002, reviewing from scratch rather than trusting the implementer's own resolution notes) re-verified all three resolutions and gave Slice 1 final acceptance -- recording one new, non-blocking Minor finding (IVM-REVIEW-F7: a `numpy.generic`-bounded-dispatch edge case that lets `numpy.complex128`/`datetime64`/`timedelta64` NaN classify as Missing; untested and currently unreachable, since nothing is wired to real ingress yet). The established Slice-1 semantic categories are String/Boolean/Number/Missing. `core.scalar_values` (`scalar_category`/`is_missing_carrier`/`is_supported_scalar`) is classification/recognition over existing carriers, not yet a canonical normalized internal scalar representation: NumPy scalar carriers (`numpy.integer`/`floating`/`bool_`/`str_`) classify into those categories without being narrowed to them, and Phase E's own value-normalization/type-resolution boundary stage still owns adding a `normalize_scalar()`-shaped primitive on top. Formula remains outside this value-model MVP, tracked durably by `FTR-FORMULA-INGRESS-ROUNDTRIP-WHITELIST-P5`. D4 (Family Cycle compatibility follow-through) remains unauthorized and unselected residual scope; the FTR itself correctly stays Open for that reason alone, not because Slice 1 is incomplete. A knowledge-anchoring pass (2026-08-09) recorded a durable, not-yet-decided architectural relationship for a future Phase-E boundary: the scalar-only MVP (String/Boolean/Number/Missing) is a current-phase scope decision, not a permanent ban on bounded composite payload values -- List[Scalar] remains a deferred extension candidate (for example a compact-cell projection under explicit codec/transformation intent, never inferred from delimiter presence in ordinary text), distinct from List[Object]/nested structured records, which stay FTR-NESTED-LISTS's structural child-frame territory. FTR-MINIMAL-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A section 16 and roadmap_domain_hardening_sequence.adoc's Phase E section were both updated with this guardrail, and FTR-NESTED-LISTS's own wording was narrowed so it no longer silently pre-decides that a list of bare scalars uses the same child-frame representation as a list of objects. `FTR-DATE-TIME-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A` (770d4dc) recorded the Phase-D current-state inventory and contract design for the Date/Time Internal Value Model: Date and DateTime as two distinct MVP scalar categories, native `datetime.date`/`datetime.datetime` as conceptual canonical carriers, `pandas.Timestamp`/`numpy.datetime64` as classified-not-narrowed carrier variants, no wrapper hierarchy, Time and Duration deferred. Independent Architecture Review 001 (17e4dd7) accepted the design with two Important findings requiring correction before implementation: DTVM-REVIEW-F1 (the FTR's own inventory misstated that non-`NaT` `numpy.timedelta64` was already rejected -- it silently misclassified as Number, independently fixed as `BUG-NUMPY-TIMEDELTA64-NUMBER-MISCLASSIFICATION-P4A`, 022f651, closed 8d32e25) and DTVM-REVIEW-F2 (the FTR's own D-T2 slice contradicted its own section 12 and Slice 1's established Phase-E-owns-normalization precedent by proposing a general `normalize_scalar()`-shaped primitive as Phase-D work). The correction pass (d41f50a) resolved both: attributed `timedelta64`'s current uniform rejection to the closed BUG rather than restating it as always-true, and removed the general normalization primitive from the Phase-D slice sequence entirely, naming it Phase E's ownership only, with D-T2 narrowed to a persistence-boundary-local carrier conversion. An independent Follow-up Review / Review Pass 002 (5270bf1) confirmed both findings RESOLVED -- independently reproducing every underlying runtime/probe claim from a fresh process -- and gave the contract final acceptance for D-T1, recording two new non-blocking Minor findings (a section-25 self-report inaccuracy about its own diff scope, and a pre-existing, unrelated `numpy.complex128` wording inconsistency in section 6, same class as the already-known `TD64-REVIEW-F1`), both corrected as pure documentation wording in 5166444 with no architecture change. Accepted contract: every supported non-`NaT` `numpy.datetime64` value classifies as DateTime regardless of unit/precision (unit-based Date inference is not merely undesirable but unreliable -- day-precision storage is bit-identically ambiguous between authored-as-date and datetime-truncated-to-day); timezone-aware `datetime.datetime`/`Timestamp` classifies as DateTime, same as naive, without `tzinfo` stripping, naive conversion, or UTC assumption (category membership only -- canonical timezone policy stays deferred to a future boundary/consumer); `numpy.timedelta64` (`NaT` or not) remains uniformly unsupported per the closed BUG, preserved by D-T1 as a non-regression, not new work; general scalar normalization/type resolution (any `normalize_scalar()`-shaped primitive, frame traversal, mandatory ingress, rejection/trust/runtime policy, boundary wiring) remains Phase E's ownership, not any D-T slice's; XLSX/ODS temporal egress/ingress parity remains explicitly deferred and ADR-gated (`ADR-VISIBLE-CELL-TYPING-STRING-SUBSTRATE` stays authoritative and unreopened), not a precondition for D-T1/D-T2/D-T3. No unresolved architecture decision blocks D-T1. See SIG-ACT-DATE-TIME-CONTRACT-ACCEPTED for the full acceptance record.
next_action: Implement and independently review D-T1 (Date/DateTime classification + explicit `datetime64` NaT handling), per the now-accepted `FTR-DATE-TIME-INTERNAL-VALUE-MODEL-P4A` contract: extend `ScalarCategory` with `"date"`/`"datetime"`; classify `datetime.date` as Date, and `datetime.datetime`/`pandas.Timestamp`/non-`NaT` `numpy.datetime64` (any unit) as DateTime, DateTime checked before Date; timezone-aware `datetime.datetime`/`Timestamp` classifies as DateTime without normalization; `numpy.datetime64('NaT')` becomes Missing through an explicit, `datetime64`-specific branch (closing the remaining half of IVM-REVIEW-F7); `numpy.timedelta64` (`NaT` or not) remains uniformly unsupported as a non-regression from the closed `BUG-NUMPY-TIMEDELTA64-NUMBER-MISCLASSIFICATION-P4A`; Time and Duration remain unsupported; no general canonical normalization primitive is built (that remains Phase E's future ownership). D-T2 (structured persistence compatibility), D-T3 (selected transformation-family compatibility pilot, still unselected), and D-T4 (spreadsheet-adapter adoption, ADR-gated) remain unauthorized and are not this concern's immediate next action. The separately-tracked, unrelated `numpy.complex128` Minor inconsistency (`TD64-REVIEW-F1`) stays deferred evidence, not a next action.
